name: bd
description: The work register: the shop's issue database, opened, commented, and closed one work item at a time by the command `bd`, its Dolt history pushed to the register's remote at session close. Use it wherever a process step opens, comments on, or closes a work item, and to push the register when a session closes.
tool_owner: no shop named — the tool's provenance as shown whoever runs it (`bd version 1.1.0 (8e4e59d39)` and its help) names none; the lead shop holds the gap as its own until an owner is found

uses.name: create
uses.description: Opens one work item in the register with the given title and prints its id. Does not close, assign, or link anything; with <dry_run> it prints what would be created and creates nothing.

title.description: the work item's title, one line

type.description: the issue type: bug, feature, task, epic, chore, or decision

priority.description: the priority, 0 (highest) to 4, or P0 to P4

description.description: the work item's description; omitted, the item has none

dry_run.description: preview only: print what would be created and create nothing

returns.text: on standard output, `✓ Created issue: <id> — <title>` then `  Priority: P<n>` and `  Status: open`, <id> the new item's id, `lead-` and five characters; with <dry_run>, `⚠ [DRY RUN] Would create issue:` and the fields, nothing created; exit status 0

failures.condition: no title was given; one line on standard error, `Error: title required (or use --file to create from markdown)`; nothing is created
failures.next: give `--title <title>` and run the invocation again

failures.condition: the arguments are not an invocation this tool states — an unknown command or flag, a flag without its value; one line on standard error beginning `Error:` says which, then the tool's usage sheet
failures.next: run the invocation the use states, as written

uses.name: comment
uses.description: Appends one comment to the work item <id>, open or closed. Changes nothing else on the item.

id.description: the work item's id, for example lead-176ti

text.description: the comment's text, quoted as one argument

returns.text: one line on standard output, `✓ Comment added to <id> — <title>`; exit status 0

failures.condition: no work item with <id> exists in the register; one line on standard error, `Error: resolving ID <id>: no issue found matching "<id>"` (`Error: resolving <id>: ...` for comment); nothing changes
failures.next: give the id of an existing work item (`lead-` and five characters, as `bd create` returned it) and run the invocation again

failures.condition: no text was given; one line on standard error, `Error: no comment text provided (use positional args, --stdin, or --file)`; nothing is added
failures.next: give the comment's text after the id and run the invocation again

failures.condition: the arguments are not an invocation this tool states — an unknown command or flag, a flag without its value; one line on standard error beginning `Error:` says which, then the tool's usage sheet
failures.next: run the invocation the use states, as written

uses.name: close
uses.description: Closes the work item <id> with the given reason, which the item keeps as its close reason. Closing an item already closed records the new reason and exits 0 as well.

id.description: the work item's id, for example lead-176ti

reason.description: why the item closes, one line, kept on the item as its close reason

returns.text: one line on standard output, `✓ Closed <id> — <title>: <reason>`; exit status 0

failures.condition: no work item with <id> exists in the register; one line on standard error, `Error: resolving ID <id>: no issue found matching "<id>"` (`Error: resolving <id>: ...` for comment); nothing changes
failures.next: give the id of an existing work item (`lead-` and five characters, as `bd create` returned it) and run the invocation again

failures.condition: the arguments are not an invocation this tool states — an unknown command or flag, a flag without its value; one line on standard error beginning `Error:` says which, then the tool's usage sheet
failures.next: run the invocation the use states, as written

uses.name: dolt-push
uses.description: Pushes the register's local Dolt commits to its configured remote (`origin`, per `bd dolt remote list`), as the session-handoff process's land step does. Pushes nothing but the register; needs a remote configured and, for a hosted remote, DOLT_REMOTE_USER and DOLT_REMOTE_PASSWORD in the environment.

returns.text: the push's report on standard output; exit status 0 — the form of the report is what the tool's help states for the push, not yet observed by this shop on this branch

failures.condition: the remote could not be written: none is configured, the credentials are missing, or the remote refuses the push; the reason on standard error — the tool's help names `--force` for a remote whose working set has uncommitted changes
failures.next: configure the remote (`bd dolt remote add <name> <url>`) or set the credentials, then run the invocation again; do not force without the lead-pm's say
